topic: How are link budgets affected when prioritizing high-revenue services versus navigation safety margins in dynamic scheduling?
consensus_response: Dynamic scheduling prioritizes revenue-generating services, increasing interference from shared spectrum. This demands intelligent channel allocation and resource prioritization strategies like DSS or QoS-aware scheduling to minimize interference and maintain service quality across competing demands.  This tradeoff requires a dynamic approach to link budgets that adapts based on real-time network conditions for optimal performance.
reference_context: Higher-revenue services demand more bandwidth, leading to increased interference from shared spectrum. This impact is evident in the need for efficient channel allocation and prioritization strategies like DSS or QoS-aware scheduling to balance competing demands.  This dynamic approach necessitates adaptive link budgets that respond to real-time network conditions.
